column1: # Ready a weapon and a shield, then reopen the equipment picker, to measure
# what `inventory.md` section 4.5 calls "a runic glyph for a readied one" in
# the selector cell - the engine leaves that cell blank for every row.
# Strength dice on the three ready beats. Character creation draws its virtue
# pairs at random (`chargen.md`; the generator is host-clock seeded,
# `prng.md §3`), so seven `a` answers do not fix the Avatar's attributes,
# and the R-Ready gate compares the readied burden against the Strength byte
# (`inventory.md §2.1`). Whether the Dagger readies or answers `Thou art not
# strong enough!` therefore depends on the draw. Measured from the Z-stats
# frames of the timelapses: rc1 (`20261017-031225`) engine Str=20, stock
# Str=20, both refused and all beats agreed; rc2 (`20261017-150213`) engine
# Str=21, stock Str=20, the engine readied the Dagger silently (panel row
# `5` with the readied glyph), the next Return unreadied it, and from there
# `dagger`, `shield` and `reopened` differed by one refusal block. A
# headless repro of the same keys at Str=20 still refuses. `picker` and
# `arms` do not depend on the draw and stay compared. The scenario wants a
# seeded save with fixed attributes to measure the readied glyph reliably.
# (rc4: the engine's own chargen draw was skewed - a quarter of its runs
# drew Strength 21 - and now uses the game-logic generator; see
# `hut-ready-refusals`. The beats stay dice at the residual ~1-in-80.)
